title: Anchor-based multi-corpus quant calibration and cosine-consistency guardrail
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reproducible, anchor-driven calibration pipeline that produces INT8/FP16 quantization profiles for embedding models and a lightweight cosine-consistency guardrail for runtime drift detection. This ticket scopes: (1) calibration orchestration across multiple corpora and batch shapes, (2) generation of per-profile statistical signatures (anchor distributions), (3) a monitoring ruleset that raises alerts when cosine similarity distributions shift beyond controlled bounds, and (4) an ops playbook for automated recalibration + rollback.
work_items: Design anchor selection strategy for multi-corpus coverage (per-corpus, cross-corpus anchors)
Implement calibration runner that records per-layer scale/zero-point and per-anchor embeddings
Compute and persist cosine-distribution signatures for each profile + dataset slice
Add monitoring detector: incremental KS test + median/90th percentile delta checks
Wire alerting into Console dashboard and create a lightweight rerun job template
Document runbook, failure modes, and automated rollback thresholds
progress_updates: 2025-11-13: Design kickoff with Applied ML and Infra. Agreed on anchor concept: 500 anchors per corpus, stratified by length and token density.
2025-11-14: Prototype calibration runner implemented (calib-runner-v0) that emits per-anchor embeddings and per-layer quant stats. Benchmarked on small internal corpus (news+docs).

2025-11-15: Early results: INT8 profiles show median cosine drop of 0.006 on NewsHoldout, FP16 shows 0.001; cross-corpus anchors expose a wider tail. Decided to add cross-batch normalization step to reduce variance.

2025-11-17: Monitoring prototype integrated with Console metrics (per-profile histogram, median and p90). Initial KS-test implementation added to detect distribution shifts; false positives observed on rolling updates — tuned window to 72h.
decisions: Use anchor-based signatures instead of only aggregate corpus statistics — gives stable paired comparisons for cosine deltas.
Primary drift detector will be a two-stage rule: (A) KS test p-value < 0.01 over last N anchors AND (B) median cosine drop > 0.005 OR p90 drop > 0.02 to trigger an alert.

Calibration outputs: store full profile artifact (scale/zeropoint per tensor), per-anchor embeddings (float32 reference, quantized restore), and summary signature (median, p25, p75, p90, KS reference distribution ID).
Automatic recalibration will be gated behind automated Canary + manual approval for Dedicated/Private customers. Hosted can opt-in to auto-recalibrate via feature flag.
risks: Anchor selection bias: anchors not representative of customer traffic may produce irrelevant alerts — mitigated by multi-corpus and traffic-derived anchors for top customers.
Operational cost: storing per-anchor embeddings for every profile can increase storage; use compressed float16 + TTL (90 days) for retention.
False positives during regular model rollouts or tokenization changes — will add rollout-aware suppression window and tokenization-version metadata on signatures.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration runner can generate INT8 and FP16 profiles for the embedding model with deterministic artifacts and a profile ID.
Anchor signatures persisted and displayed in Console for at least three holdout corpora (news, wiki, support-tickets).
Drift detector triggers at <=2% false positive rate in a simulated 30-day rolling test and detects injected 0.01 median cosine regression in synthetic attack tests within 24h.
Ops runbook documented and tested: automated recalibration job can be started from Console and a rollback path exists that restores previous profile within 15 minutes.
Storage policy implemented: per-anchor embeddings compressed to float16, TTL default 90 days, opt-out for enterprise customers.
notes: Prototype showed benefit from an additional per-anchor centering step: subtract per-anchor mean before cosine computation to reduce token-length skew.
Consider adding a lightweight embedding sketch (1KB Bloom-like projection) for long-term retention instead of raw per-anchor vectors to further reduce storage.
Follow-up: run a calibration stress job across 10 customer corpora and produce a heatmap of profile stability by model-version + sequence-length bucket.
